executive_summary.summary: The workflow begins when a manager submits an access request and proceeds through intake completeness checks, employee and manager verification, access-characteristic classification, clarification where needed, application-owner decision, conditional security review, human provisioning, ticket and evidence update, SLA escalation, and weekly reporting. The workflow is suitable for a constrained read-only advisory pilot that uses approved derived fields to identify deficiencies, prepare reviewer packets, flag routing needs, and support SLA visibility. It is not ready for autonomous decisions, provisioning, record updates, communications, escalation, or report distribution because these actions require human authority, evidence, and audit controls. Overall readiness score: 74/100.
primary_value_opportunities: Map workflow fields to policy-classified elements, resolve differences such as system_requested versus requested_system and employee_status versus employment_status, and approve a deny-by-default model-context allowlist. Treat unresolved mappings as blocked.

Create a controlled view containing only approved normalized and derived signals. Exclude raw PII, sensitive access details, free text, provisioning actions, approval evidence, and provisioning records, and retain a model-input filtering log.

Encode intake completeness, HR verification, security-review routing, and approval completeness in controlled workflow logic. The model should consume resulting statuses and produce advisory summaries only.

Use the model to identify model-safe deficiencies, assemble status summaries, flag potential additional review, and draft reviewer packets without sending messages or writing to any system. Compare outputs with human decisions and corrections.

Provide separate review queues for clarification, application-owner decisions, security review, provisioning, ticket updates, SLA escalations, and report distribution. Execution should occur only after the documented human approval and evidence requirements are satisfied.
primary_constraints: Restricted data could enter model context through raw tickets, HR attributes, free text, access details, or evidence attachments.
Incorrect access classification could omit a required security review.
Provisioning could occur based on an incomplete or oversimplified approval state.
Model-generated ticket changes, clarification requests, escalation notices, or report distribution could bypass approval and audit requirements.
Unclear SLA thresholds and routing recipients could produce late, premature, or misdirected escalation recommendations.

The exact required intake schema, validation rules, and acceptable values are not fully specified. STEP-001 names employee, application, role, access scope, and business justification, but the packet does not provide a complete field-level intake contract. Evidence: DOC-002, DOC-005.
The authoritative definitions and routing logic for sensitive, custom, API, SSO, security-impacting, and emergency access are not fully documented. Evidence: DOC-002, DOC-003, DOC-004.
SLA thresholds, business calendars, escalation timing, authorized recipients, and handling rules for low, medium, and high sla_risk are not provided. Evidence: DOC-002, DOC-004, DOC-006.

Retrieve applicable policy, control, and approval requirements.
Classify workflow fields by sensitivity and required handling controls.
Check whether workflow intake contains required fields and flag incomplete or conflicting information.

implementation_roadmap.title: Read-only workflow intelligence
implementation_roadmap.objective: Introduce AI assistance for summarization, evidence review, policy lookup, and gap detection without allowing workflow writes.
recommended_actions: Connect approved workflow and policy documents through governed retrieval.
Review data sensitivity and missing information findings.
exit_criteria: Analysis output passes quality, MCP operational, and evidence-grounding checks.
Business reviewers confirm the output is useful and sufficiently grounded.

implementation_roadmap.title: Human-reviewed AI recommendations
implementation_roadmap.objective: Allow AI to prepare recommendations, reviewer summaries, and approval packages while keeping decisions with accountable humans.
recommended_actions: Define reviewer roles and approval gates.
Add structured review queues for AI-prepared recommendations.
Track acceptance, rejection, and revision reasons.
exit_criteria: Reviewers can trace recommendations to evidence.

implementation_roadmap.title: Approval-gated workflow actions
implementation_roadmap.objective: Introduce controlled write actions only where approvals, policy checks, and audit logging are enforced.
recommended_actions: Implement policy checks before write-capable tools.
Require explicit approval tokens for controlled actions.
Log every write attempt, approval, and result.
exit_criteria: No write-capable tool can execute without required approval.
Audit trail is complete and reviewable.

implementation_roadmap.title: Limited automation for low-risk repeatable actions
implementation_roadmap.objective: Consider limited automation only for well-documented, low-risk steps with clear rollback and monitoring.
recommended_actions: Run parallel monitoring before autonomous execution.
exit_criteria: Automation scope is narrow and documented.
Monitoring confirms accuracy, safety, and cost expectations.

expected_cost_drivers: LLM calls for workflow analysis and blueprint generation.
Model reasoning effort and context size.
Repeated evaluation runs during testing or model comparison.
cost_controls: Use premium models only for milestone quality gates.
Use cheaper models for schema, parsing, and smoke tests where appropriate.
Cache workflow packet context and evidence catalogs when inputs have not changed.
Track model usage, latency, and estimated cost per run.
operational_controls: Require governed tool access through MCP or equivalent policy-controlled interfaces.
Log tool calls, approvals, artifact generation, and write attempts.
Fail closed when policy, evidence, or approval requirements are missing.
observability_requirements: Model provider, model name, reasoning effort, token usage, and latency.
Evaluation scores for quality, MCP operation, and evidence grounding.

limitations_and_missing_information: The exact required intake schema, validation rules, and acceptable values are not fully specified. STEP-001 names employee, application, role, access scope, and business justification, but the packet does not provide a complete field-level intake contract. Evidence: DOC-002, DOC-005.
The authoritative definitions and routing logic for sensitive, custom, API, SSO, security-impacting, and emergency access are not fully documented. Evidence: DOC-002, DOC-003, DOC-004.
SLA thresholds, business calendars, escalation timing, authorized recipients, and handling rules for low, medium, and high sla_risk are not provided. Evidence: DOC-002, DOC-004, DOC-006.
The authoritative source for determining whether an Application Owner is authorized, including delegation and unavailable-owner handling, is not specified. Evidence: DOC-002, DOC-003.

Retention periods and approved repositories for request tickets, model-input logs, approvals, security outcomes, provisioning evidence, audit events, and weekly reports are not stated beyond general retention instructions. Evidence: DOC-003.

The canonical mapping and precedence between similarly named workflow and policy fields, including system_requested/requested_system and employee_status/employment_status, are unresolved. Evidence: DOC-005, POLICY-001.
The permitted authentication scopes, service-account permissions, credential management, and technical audit interfaces for the write-capable target systems are not documented. Evidence: DOC-007.
Operational performance baselines and acceptable safety thresholds for missed deficiencies, unsupported recommendations, and routing errors are not fully established. Evidence: DOC-006.
The report audience, approved distribution channels, sensitivity determination method, and required report template are not specified. Evidence: DOC-002, DOC-003, DOC-007.

The required-control service returned no control mappings for the queried governed actions, so the relationship between the packet controls and the broader policy catalog remains unresolved. Evidence: DOC-003, POLICY-002.

The five targeted searches returned no additional results; therefore, no supplementary evidence was retrieved for approval routing, SLA rules, audit retention, clarification handling, or HR verification details beyond the packet documents. Evidence: DOC-001, DOC-002, DOC-003, POLICY-002.
